name: DPRODUCT
description: DPRODUCT multiplies the numeric values in a specified field of the database records that match the given criteria.
tldr: Multiplies the values in a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to multiply, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are multiplied.

basicExample.description: Multiply the Yield of apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:B10 (Tree=Apple, Height>10) matches two rows with Yield 14 and 10; multiplying gives 14 x 10 = 140.

advancedExamples.title: Multiply Profit for the same trees
advancedExamples.description: Use the same criteria but multiply the Profit column instead.
advancedExamples.explanation: The two matching rows have Profit 105 and 75, so 105 x 75 = 7875.

advancedExamples.title: Three factors from all apple trees
advancedExamples.description: Multiply the Yield of all three apple rows.
advancedExamples.explanation: Apple yields are 14, 10, and 6, so the product is 14 x 10 x 6 = 840.

howItWorks: DPRODUCT filters the database to rows matching the criteria, then multiplies together the numeric values found in the specified field column of those rows. Text and blank cells in the field are ignored; if no numeric values match, the product is 0 (since the implicit starting factor is 1 only when at least one value exists, but Excel treats zero matches as 0).

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Considers only numeric values in the field; text and blanks are ignored.
With many values the product can quickly overflow to very large numbers.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.

commonErrors.cause: No rows matched, or the matching field contained no numeric values.
commonErrors.fix: Verify the criteria headers and conditions match the database and that the field holds numbers.

commonErrors.cause: The field was an unquoted column name.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Yield", or use the column index.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DPRODUCT works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior.

faq.question: What does DPRODUCT return if no rows match?
faq.answer: It returns 0, because there are no numeric values to multiply.

faq.question: Does DPRODUCT ignore text in the field?
faq.answer: Yes. Only numeric values in matching rows are multiplied.

faq.question: When is DPRODUCT useful?
faq.answer: It is handy for compounding rates or factors stored in a database column across matching records.
